page.description: Redox OS editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A Unix-like operating system written in Rust, with its own kernel and userspace, aiming at a microkernel-inspired design with memory safety throughout.
pros: Written in Rust from the kernel up.
Scheme-like design: drivers and services run in userspace.
Runs on x86_64 and i686, with daily images between releases.
cons: 0.9.0 is from September 2024; daily images carry newer code.
Media ships zstd-compressed, so decompress before writing it.
A small community compared with mainstream systems.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for Redox OS; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Redox publishes zstd-compressed livedisk and harddrive images. Decompress an image with zstd, then write it to a stick or a virtual disk; writing erases the target device.

editions.name: Desktop
editions.description: The desktop image, with the Redox Orbital desktop and the core applications.
editions.usbNote: 115 MB zstd-compressed ISO for x86_64, 115 MB for i686. Decompress it, then write it to a stick.

editions.name: Server
editions.description: A smaller image with the server tooling and no desktop.
editions.usbNote: 70 MB zstd-compressed ISO. Decompress it, then write it to a stick.

editions.name: Demo
editions.description: A demonstration image with sample applications and less of the desktop tooling.
editions.usbNote: 344 MB zstd-compressed ISO for x86_64, 170 MB for i686. Decompress it, then write it to a stick.
